clue.text: Remove upper-class chap on vehicle

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece sitting on another follows it, so the chap comes after the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a toff is British slang for a posh, upper-class man

explanation.surface: Someone is told to get rid of a posh fellow perched on a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: A toff is British slang for a posh man. In an across clue 'on' means after, so the chap follows the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To haul something away is to remove it, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Grab eggs from a nest

definitions.meaning: to grab is to seize or snatch at something
a set of eggs laid together by one bird is known by this word

explanation.definitionFit: A grasping snatch and a whole brood of eggs share the same word: one verb, one noun for a bird's sitting.

clue.text: Musician's performance of clarinet arrangement, not new

indicators.note: an arrangement in music reworks a piece, so these letters are reordered
not new tells us to drop the abbreviation for new from the instrument's letters

explanation.surface: A clarinettist gives a concert using a fresh arrangement of an old piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not new' strips N from CLARINET, leaving CLARIET; 'arrangement' rearranges those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo concert given by one player is a standard name for a musician's performance.

clue.text: Excess liquid proves unusually damaging

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters of proves set out in an unusual order

parts.note: ill can mean harmful or damaging, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: Too much fluid turns out to cause unusual harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaging' looks like an adjective tied to 'proves', but it supplies a separate piece: ill, as in 'ill effects'.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that floods beyond its container is the overflow or surplus, so excess liquid.

clue.text: By good luck, seeing that large cask in cathedral city

parts.note: for can mean because or seeing that, as in 'for it was late'
a tun is a large barrel for wine or beer
at can mean in, as in 'at Paris'
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England

explanation.surface: A lucky find: a huge barrel turns up in an English cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: ELY is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, a crossword favourite; 'in' gives AT.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb meaning luckily or happily, describing what happens through chance in one's favour.

clue.text: Expert making obvious comment about temperature

definitions.meaning: a highly skilled or successful person, an ace
read as '...', a statement of the obvious about heat

explanation.definitionFit: An ace or high-flier is called this, and split up it reads as a truism about heat.

clue.text: Old boat that's said to attract attention

definitions.meaning: a small coastal sailing vessel of former times went by this name
an interjection shouted to catch someone's notice, like 'oi' or 'ahoy'

explanation.definitionFit: The name of a historic small sailing vessel is also an old cry used to hail someone.

clue.text: Instrument to collect tax, by law — endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly applies to each of the three words, dropping the final letter of every one

parts.note: the three words are taken as written, each to be cut short

explanation.surface: A device for gathering levies that the law has authorised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims all three words: TA(x), B(y), LA(w) run together give the answer; 'to collect' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of small Indian hand drums is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Hard speech cut in part of Hamlet

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: cut means the speech loses its final letter

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A tough speech is trimmed in a production of Shakespeare's play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes the last letter of ORATION. 'part' here means a role in the play, not a section of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's loyal friend is a role in Shakespeare's tragedy, so a part to be played.

clue.text: Oriental food one Tibetan native used in strange rite

indicators.note: used in means the next pieces are placed inside the rearranged letters
strange signals the letters of rite set in an odd order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
the yak is an ox native to Tibet

explanation.surface: An Asian dish involving a Tibetan beast at some peculiar ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges the four letters of rite to TERI; 'used in' slips the next pieces in before its final I.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese style of grilled meat glazed in sweet soy sauce is an Eastern dish.

clue.text: Without good definition of Lear's aged relative

definitions.meaning: an adverb meaning vaguely or indistinctly, not sharply defined
Edward Lear wrote a nonsense poem about the elderly ...

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lear' suggests King Lear, but it is Edward Lear, the nonsense poet, whose poem concerns 'my aged Uncle Arly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Done vaguely or blurrily, lacking sharpness, matches 'without good definition'.

clue.text: Uninteresting type of creature entering wood

definitions.meaning: one who bores people, a tedious person
an insect or worm that drills its way into timber

explanation.definitionFit: A tedious person who bores, and an insect that drills tunnels in timber, share the name.

clue.text: Pierce one's skin

parts.note: to cut can mean to pierce or penetrate
one gives I, the Roman numeral, and 's gives is

explanation.surface: A command to puncture someone's hide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is': I plus IS's S, giving IS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin anatomical term for the true skin, the dermis, used in medicine.

clue.text: Left inside any hut, he adapted poorly

indicators.note: inside places the abbreviation within the rearranged letters
adapted means the letters of any hut, he are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A man who never got used to life in a shack ended up sickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' rearranges ANYHUTHE and 'inside' puts L within it; 'poorly' is British for unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Poorly in British usage means unwell, so not in good health.

clue.text: Crushed earth?

parts.note: the word earth is what you get from the letters of heart when they are broken up and rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as wordplay, tells you to break HEART, which gives EARTH, the clue word.
explanation.definitionFit: Crushed by grief or disappointment means devastated, an emotional sense.

clue.text: Rome's construction wasn't routine

definitions.meaning: Rome wasn't built in a day, so building it was no single shift's task
routine means ordinary, part of the normal daily job

explanation.walkthrough: It plays on the proverb 'Rome wasn't built in a day'.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase for a task that is nothing special, just the normal daily grind, fits 'routine'.

clue.text: One naturally bakes new buns with 13

indicators.note: new signals that buns is remade with its letters reordered

parts.note: 13-down's answer instructs us to break up the word heart, giving these letters

explanation.surface: Someone's oven-baking fresh buns along with a broken heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges BUNS to SUNB. '13' borrows the answer to 13-down: HEART broken, here as ATHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lying out in the sun is cooked by natural heat, browning like a loaf.

clue.text: To beat, in motion?

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to thrash or beat them
going means moving, in motion

explanation.surface: A question about striking someone while on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines it: dancing an Argentine ballroom dance is moving to a beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Dancing the Argentine ballroom dance means moving rhythmically to the music's pulse.

clue.text: An extremely hostile aim towards part of leg

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, which shortens to a
chill can mean cold and unfriendly, so its superlative means most hostile
an end is a goal or aim, as in 'ends and means'
on can mean towards, as in 'march on Rome'

explanation.surface: Someone takes very unfriendly aim at a leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely hostile' gives the superlative CHILLEST (from chill, cold and unfriendly), not an outer-letters pick.
explanation.definitionFit: The cord joining the calf muscle to the heel bone is part of the lower leg.

clue.text: Da, for example, calling for shock treatment

definitions.meaning: a DA, short for duck's arse, is a 1950s slicked-back hairstyle
a shock is a thick mass of hair, so its treatment is a trim

explanation.walkthrough: A DA (duck's arse) is a greased-back 1950s hairstyle; 'shock' means a mop of hair, not electrical therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: A trim or styling of the head is both an example like a DA and what a mop of hair receives.

clue.text: In ring situation, black and blue

indicators.note: In means the letter for black goes inside the ring and setting run together

parts.note: O is a ring, from its shape
a scene can mean a setting or situation
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A boxer in the ring ends up with a black and blue face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' means indecent here, not a colour; 'black and blue' looks like bruising.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue jokes or films are smutty, indecent ones, an informal sense.

clue.text: China — antique article girl's holding

indicators.note: holding means the girl's name wraps around the article

parts.note: Cathy is a girl's name
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A girl clutching an antique piece of porcelain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like porcelain beside 'antique', but it is the country, and 'antique' says the name is old.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval European name for China, made familiar by Marco Polo, is an archaic term.

clue.text: Person who denies making profit, for example, with royalty

parts.note: a gain is a profit
say is used to introduce an example, as in 'a fruit, say an apple'
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of denying they made money, among other things, with the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to contradict or deny, so one who does it is a denier.

clue.text: Child told to get out of bed early in America

indicators.note: told signals the word is spoken, so we take what it sounds like

parts.note: a son is a child
up means out of bed, risen

explanation.surface: A youngster is instructed to rise from bed early, American style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'told' makes SON into its sound-alike; 'early in America' means daybreak in American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: American English for dawn, the early-morning moment of sunrise.

clue.text: Where Corcoran was hardly ever sick or confused

definitions.text: Where Corcoran was hardly ever sick
definitions.meaning: Captain Corcoran in Gilbert and Sullivan's HMS Pinafore sings that he is hardly ever sick on the ocean
an idiom for bewildered, out of one's depth

explanation.walkthrough: Captain Corcoran in Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera HMS Pinafore boasts he is 'hardly ever sick' while sailing.
explanation.definitionFit: Out on the ocean is where the captain sails, and the idiom means bewildered.

clue.text: Like some south Americans captured on film

definitions.meaning: relating to the Inca people of Peru
a film shot and finished is said to be 'in the can'

explanation.walkthrough: 'In the can' is film-making slang for completed footage.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the Inca empire of the Andes describes some South Americans; split, it means filmed.

clue.text: Gift of money returned, we hear — he's doubly confused

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: back means returned, as in 'she's back'

indicators.note: confused signals that the doubled letters are jumbled
doubly means the letters of he's are taken twice

explanation.surface: A man returns a cash present, the story goes, utterly bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' makes BACK into BAK; 'doubly' gives HESHES and 'confused' rearranges it to SHEESH.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip or bribe given in parts of Asia and the Middle East is a gratuity of money.

clue.text: Save from capsized boat

indicators.note: capsized means turned upside down, so in a down clue the word is read upwards

parts.note: a tub is a slang name for a slow, clumsy boat

explanation.surface: A rescue from an overturned vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' looks like rescue, but it means except, as in 'all save one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Save as a preposition means except, as in 'everyone save me'.

clue.text: Deteriorate, as stakes do

definitions.meaning: to decline or fall into ruin
gamblers' stakes are placed into the pool of bets on the table

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for going to ruin also literally describes bets heading into the pool.

clue.text: Where trees are tended — but not elders?

definitions.meaning: a place where young plants and saplings are raised
a room for small children rather than grown-ups; elder is also a tree

explanation.walkthrough: 'elders' doubles as the elder tree, which suits the trees of the first half.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant-raising business and a room for young children share one name.
